newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of April 7, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - Advanced Micro Inc can claim it has the fastest X86 processor today with its K6 chip but when the Pentium II arrives next month, Intel will reclaim the lead, PC Week reported in a review of the two processors April 7.

Sybase Inc will unveil this week a bundle of tools designed to make it easier to move information into a data warehouse, along with an upgrade of its Sybase IQ databases that speeds query processing, PC Week reported.

COMPUTERWORLD - Wireless access to the Internet is becoming more widely available for mobile users and companies. WarpDrive Networks plans next week to announce beta testing of a wireless Internet service, scheduled to launch in San Jose and Seattle in June. Also, Metrocom Inc and World Wireless Communications Inc have plans for wireless access, ComputerWorld reported April 7.
COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Developers and valued-added resellers are wary of Oracle Corp's network computer architecture plan because it seems incomplete.

They said there was no clear definition of what constitutes a cartridge and no certification process in place to ensure the cartridges work together. Oracle said they are working on defining the NC architecture but said certification is not necessarily needed, Computer Reseller News reported April 7.

INFOWORLD - With Java virtual machines gaining wide acceptance, computer scientists are focusing on universal virtual machines, which would theoretically allow developers to write applications in any language and run them on any machine, InfoWorld reported April 7.

INFORMATION WEEK - Rising labor costs could force analysts to revise upward the estimate that Year 2000 compliance will costs companies between $300 billion and $600 billion, Information Week reported April 7.
Internet service providers are encountering problems with Digital Equipment Corp's GigaSwitch FDDI, which can drop data packets in heavy traffic, Information Week reported April 7.

EE TIMES - Intel Corp will move the complete base of electronic design automation, or EDA, technology it uses to develop its chips to Microsoft Corp's Windows NT and off of UNIX, a move seen as an endorsement of Microsoft's operating system, EE Times said in its April 7 issue.

Aerospace executives at a Colorado Space Symposium last week warned that a vast expansion of available satellite launch services must be soon undertaken if the telecommunications industry is to meet global demand, EE Times reported April 7.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS NEWS - Industry analysts say that Intel Corp will respond to Advanced Micro Devices Inc's new K6 chip by releasig the Pentium II chip, lowering prices in August and possibly giving the cold shoulder to original equipment manufacturers, or OEMs, who use AMD products, Electronic Buyers news reported April 7.

Hewlett-Packard Inc and Singapore's state-owned Chartered Semiconductor Manufacturing have formed a joint venture to build eight-inch silicon wafers adjacent to Chartered's existing plants, Electronic Buyers News reported April 7. The new plant will go into operation in 1999.
MAC WEEK - Soon after shedding the Performa label, Apple Computer Inc has taken the wraps off three entry-level Macs, including the first-ever model with a 300 megahertz PowerPC processor.
Apple also introduced a pair of 166-MHz PC Compatibility cards meant to improve Windows performance on the Mac, MacWeek reported on April 7.
